ov: Six species of air-breathing freshwater fish in Africa, South America and Australia, the closest living relatives of land vertebrates. Their lobed fins have a bony skeleton inside, and their fossil record goes back more than 410 million years.
len: Up to 2 m (marbled lungfish, the largest African species)
rg: Africa, South America and Australia; lungfish once lived all over the world.
df: Crustaceans, worms, molluscs, amphibians and plant matter, crushed with tooth plates.
fx: An Australian lungfish called Granddad lived at Chicago's Shedd Aquarium from 1933 to 2017 and died at about 109.
The Australian lungfish has only one lung; the other species have two.
